text:
Emily Chen: Quick design review — the trial credits expiry banner that shows in the top-right. Need copy that feels urgent but not alarmist. Current draft: 'Your trial credits expire in 7 days — upgrade to avoid interruption.' Thoughts?
Jordan Park: I like the directness. Two quick nit ideas: (1) shorten to '7 days left on your trial' for scannability; (2) call out action: 'Upgrade to continue' vs 'Upgrade to avoid interruption' — second sounds a bit scary.
Samir Patel: Agree with Jordan — shorter is better for banners. Maybe: '7 days left — upgrade to keep using Redwood' (keeps friendly tone).
Olga Kuznetsova: Accessibility notes: banner should be in a region with `aria-live="polite"` by default so screen readers announce it without interrupting. For the CTA, make sure button text is explicit (not just 'Upgrade') — use 'Upgrade plan' or 'Upgrade to paid' so context is clear when read out of line.
Rohit Desai: Implementation constraints: we have 60 char limit before truncation on small viewports. Also need to support i18n placeholders. Example with variables: `{{days_left}} days left — Upgrade to continue`
Emily Chen: Good call on CTA wording. So candidate set: 
- Short: "7 days left — Upgrade plan"
- Friendly: "7 days left — Upgrade to keep using Redwood"
- Urgency but softer: "Trial ends in 7 days — upgrade to keep access"
Which one should we A/B?
Jordan Park: I'd A/B Short vs Friendly. Short for power users, Friendly for new/dev users. Also propose adding a subtle secondary link 'View usage' to help people who might have credits but still think it's unexpected.
Olga Kuznetsova: For screen readers, suggest adding visually-hidden extra text on the CTA with `aria-hidden="false"`? No — better: include `sr-only` text that reads 'opens billing page' after CTA, e.g., 'Upgrade plan — opens billing settings'. Keep the visible CTA short but ensure the accessible name is explicit.
Samir Patel: UI nit: add an icon (clock) to the left — helps draw attention. But please check with marketing/brand on tone first.
Rohit Desai: Dev note: when days_left <= 1 change copy to singular: '1 day left' and for 0 -> 'Your trial has expired' (different banner state). Need copy for that case too.
Emily Chen: OK drafting final variants: 
1) "{{days_left}} days left — Upgrade plan" + CTA text: "Upgrade plan" (aria-label: "Upgrade plan, opens billing settings")
2) "{{days_left}} days left — Upgrade to keep using Redwood" + CTA: "Upgrade" (aria-label: "Upgrade to paid plan, opens billing settings")
3) Expired state: "Your trial has ended" + CTA: "View billing options" (aria-label: "View billing options, opens billing settings")
Can design/ux pick 1 & 2 for A/B and ops add the SR aria-labels?
Jordan Park: Sounds good. I'll set up the A/B in Figma and share frames. Emily can you add a microcopy card in the PR with exact strings and i18n keys?
Emily Chen: Yep will add copy to PR + include translations note. Anyone object to CTA verb being 'Upgrade plan' vs 'Upgrade'?
Samir Patel: Prefer 'Upgrade plan' as it's clearer when truncated or read by screen reader.
Olga Kuznetsova: Agree. Also prefer `aria-live="polite"` and for the expired state use `aria-live="assertive"` since it's a state change that affects access.
product-bot: A/B test scaffold created — test id TB-4482. Variants: short vs friendly.
Rohit Desai: I'll implement truncation fallback and make sure aria-labels use full copy from i18n keys, not the visible truncated string.
Emily Chen: Thanks all — I'll push copy change in the branch later today and tag @marketing for tone review. :thumbsup:
